title: NFTStakerMigrator stores a dead immutable stakedId never referenced by migrate(); implies a parity guarantee the code does not enforce
description: NFTStakerMigrator stores an immutable stakedId (L44/L62) that migrate() never references and never asserts equal across the old/new stakers. A cross-staker stakedId mismatch surfaces only as a hard revert with clean atomic rollback (no partial state, no fund loss). The dead immutable is misleading — it implies a parity guarantee the code does not enforce. Distinct contract and distinct failure mode from the InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator strand (clean DoS-revert with rollback here vs the silent floor/hatch drift there).
impact: None. Worst case is a self-evident revert at migration time with clean atomic rollback; operator observes a failed migration and re-deploys with correct wiring. QA hardening.
attackPath: 1. Deploy NFTStakerMigrator with a stakedId that does not match one of the wired stakers (or the stakers disagree).
2. Call migrate(): the ERC1155 move reverts on the id mismatch; the whole call rolls back atomically.
3. No funds move; operator re-deploys with correct wiring.
recommendation: Either wire the immutable into a real cross-staker parity assert in migrate() (require the source/destination stakers agree with the migrator's stakedId), or remove the dead immutable to avoid implying an unenforced guarantee.
